questions.prompt: What is a key difference between a Promise and an Observable?

options.text: Promises can emit many values; Observables emit exactly one
An Observable is lazy, can emit many values over time, and is cancellable via unsubscribe()
Promises support operators like map and filter

questions.explanation: A Promise is eager and single-value; an Observable is lazy (runs on subscribe), multi-value, and cancellable.

questions.prompt: What does the async pipe do in a template?

options.text: Converts an Observable into a Promise
Subscribes, shows the latest value, and unsubscribes automatically when the component is destroyed
Runs the Observable only once and caches it forever
Adds error handling to the stream

questions.explanation: The async pipe manages the subscription lifecycle for you, preventing leaks and removing manual subscribe/unsubscribe.

questions.prompt: Which operator cancels a previous in-flight HTTP request when a new search term arrives?
questions.explanation: switchMap cancels the previous inner Observable and switches to the newest — ideal for typeahead search.

questions.prompt: Match each flattening operator to its behavior.

pairs.right: Cancel the old, use the new
Run in order, one at a time

questions.explanation: Choosing the right flattening operator prevents race conditions and duplicate submissions.

questions.prompt: For a manual subscription in component logic, what's the modern way to avoid a memory leak without ngOnDestroy boilerplate?
questions.explanation: takeUntilDestroyed() ties the subscription to the component's DestroyRef and completes it on destroy.

questions.prompt: By convention, variable names holding Observables are suffixed with which single character (e.g. user__)?
questions.explanation: The $ suffix (user$, results$) is a widely adopted convention that makes Observables easy to spot.

questions.prompt: You call takeUntilDestroyed() with no argument inside ngOnInit(). What happens?

options.text: It works, because the component uses inject()
It throws: ngOnInit is not an injection context, so pass a DestroyRef injected in a field

questions.explanation: Without an argument, takeUntilDestroyed() injects DestroyRef itself, which only works in a constructor or field initializer. In ngOnInit, use takeUntilDestroyed(this.destroyRef).
